raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

A full HF3FS page pool makes every save fail permanently: once
`allocate_pages_for_keys` runs out of pages there is no way to get one back and
the metadata server has to be restarted (issue #62389).

#62393 stops cache hits and duplicate keys from consuming *new* pages, but it
deliberately does not add eviction, so the failure above remains.

Naively evicting the least-recently-used key is unsafe here: the scheduler calls
`batch_key_exists` (via `get_num_new_matched_tokens`) before the worker loads the
block (`get_key_locations`), so a key can be a "hit" while its page is still
about to be read. Recycling that page turns a hit into a load failure or into
another request's data.

## Stacked on #62393

This branch is based on #62393 (`84f00fa`) because the two changes touch the same
allocation path. The first commit in the diff is #62393 itself; **only the second
commit is new here**. I will rebase onto `main` once #62393 lands.

## What this does

- **Reader leases.** `POST /keys/acquire` returns page locations *and* pins the
  keys; `POST /keys/release` drops the pin. The load path
  (`AsyncOperationManager._handle_load_task`) acquires before reading and
  releases as soon as the blocks are in host buffers: on success, on a missing
  key, on read failure, and on exceptions.
- **LRU eviction of safe keys only.** When allocation needs more pages than the
  free list has, the server reclaims complete, unleased keys that are not part of
  the allocating request (`exclude=cached_pages`), oldest first, returning one
  page per rank to the free list and deleting the key.
- **Lease expiry.** Leases carry a monotonic deadline (default 120 s,
  `--lease-ttl-s`) so a crashed reader cannot pin pages forever. The TTL is a
  safety parameter, not a tuning knob: it has to exceed the slowest block load.
  Reported figures in #62389: a 28k-token prompt loads in about 1.1 s and a 60k
  one in about 1.9 s, but a failed 3FS storage pod stalled loads for 16-18 s, so
  the 120 s default leaves roughly 7x headroom over the observed stall. Renewal
  for loads longer than the TTL is not implemented; a reader that stalls longer
  than the TTL is treated as dead.
- **Backward compatible.** `Hf3fsMetadataInterface.acquire_keys/release_keys`
  have non-abstract defaults (plain lookup / no-op), so the mock and single-node
  clients are unaffected. The HTTP client falls back to `get_key_locations` on
  404/405, which is safe against an older server because it never evicts.

## Correctness argument

- A page is only handed out after it is back in the free list; eviction releases
  it there first.
- Only complete keys are tracked for eviction; partial keys stay owned by their
  writer (the boundary with #61247).
- A key with a live lease is never evicted; its owner releases it or it expires.
- Eviction cannot target the allocating request's own hits, so a batch that has
  already decided to read a page cannot recycle it underneath itself.

## Testing

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_metadata_server.py` gains 7 cases:
  eviction makes room, leases protect, expired leases are reclaimed, partial keys
  are skipped, same-request hits are not evicted, LRU order respects acquires,
  and eviction returns one page per rank.
- Isolated harness (full source plus upstream tests, only the import path
  rewritten, `--noconftest`): **25 passed**, then a real localhost HTTP probe
  that leases every complete key, asserts allocation fails, releases one key,
  and asserts the eviction landed on that key.

## Not verified here

- Two vLLM instances sharing one metadata server on real 3FS (needs a 3FS setup;
  @sivabreddy offered to run it).
- The writer-side boundary with #61247.
- Eviction cost and hit-rate impact: this PR is about correctness, not policy.
- Connector-level unit tests were not run on the authoring machine (the review
  environment has no torch/GPU); the connector change is small and was read by
  hand. `pre-commit` has not been run yet either.

## AI assistance

The implementation and this description were drafted with an AI coding agent
(see the `Assisted-by` trailer). I am opening it as a draft for design feedback.

🚀

Test results on real 3FS, as offered in #62389.

**Setup:** vLLM v0.32.0 with the two changed files of this PR at `ed8a5db` (the PR base is identical to v0.32.0 for these files), plus the one-line metadata URL fix from #62465 (without it each instance talks to a localhost metadata server). Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, TP4, block size 64. Two instances on two H100 hosts (pod A writes, pod B reads), one shared metadata server (this PR's file, default lease TTL 120 s), 3FS over FUSE with USRBIO. Small pool on purpose: `hf3fs_file_size` 2 GiB per rank = 409 pages per rank. Needle prompts of about 1,850 tokens with one known answer each; flood prompts of 3,256 tokens (50 new keys each).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Before the pool is full | B loaded A's prompts from 3FS (1,792 of 1,850 tokens), answers correct |
| Sequential flood past the pool (12 prompts) | each prompt evicted exactly 50 keys; free pages stayed 0 on all 4 ranks; B loaded the 3 newest prompts from 3FS (3,200 tokens each) |
| Concurrent flood (12 prompts, 8 at a time) | B loaded the 3 newest prompts from 3FS (3,200 tokens each) |
| New prompts after the pool is full | 4 of 4 stored and loaded by B from 3FS (1,792-1,856 tokens), answers correct |
| Old prompts | stored before the flood: evicted (0 tokens from 3FS on B), answers correct (recomputed) |
| Lease protects keys | I held a lease with `POST /keys/acquire` on all 4 ranks for one prompt's 29 keys and never released it (a stalled reader), then flooded: an unleased control prompt had 0 of 29 keys left, the leased prompt 29 of 29; B loaded the leased prompt from 3FS (1,792 tokens), answer correct |
| Expired lease | 134 s after the acquire, the next flood evicted the leased prompt (0 of 29 keys), `leased` count 0 |
| Errors | 0 failed saves and 0 failed loads in the vLLM KV transfer metrics on both instances; 0 wrong answers in 28 needle checks |

Two observations:

1. The lease deadline is the latest deadline of all leases on a key. B read the leased prompt about 10 s after my acquire, so at 125 s 28 of the 29 keys still counted as leased, and they were evicted at 134 s. So a lease that is never released lasts until no reader has touched the key for one TTL. I think that is fine; it may be worth a line in the docs.
2. Seen once and not reproduced: 15 s after a larger concurrent flood (60 prompts, 8 at a time, about 5 x the pool), B found none of the 3 newest prompts, and free pages were 100 on rank 0 and 50 on ranks 1-3. The 12-prompt floods above did not show it. Saves may still have been in progress; I did not prove the cause.

Not covered: a real reader process killed in the middle of a read (I simulated the stalled reader with `/keys/acquire`), and throughput impact.

Thanks for running this on real 3FS with two hosts - that covers the two things I could not test here (two writers, one metadata server, and a pool that actually fills). The numbers answer what a single-host harness cannot: each flood prompt evicting exactly its 50 keys, 0/29 unleased vs 29/29 leased surviving, and the expired lease reclaimed on the next flood.

On (1): you are right, and it is now written down. Leases are counted per key, and a key stays pinned until the latest deadline among its live leases, so one reader releasing does not unpin it for another reader. Your 125 s observation is the same rule seen from the other side: pod B's read at ~10 s refreshed the deadline, so the pin lasted until last-touch + TTL, not acquire + TTL. I added that sentence to `acquire_keys` and a test (`test_overlapping_leases_keep_the_key_pinned`: acquire with 10 s, then 1e6 s, release the first, require that allocation still fails; release the second, require that it succeeds). Pushed as c9b2b40 - docstring and test only, no behaviour change, so the sha moves from ed8a5db to c9b2b40. Local isolated harness: 26 passed, ruff clean. Any test you re-run on c9b2b40 is testing the same code paths.

On (2) I do not have a proven explanation either. The 100/50 free-page split plus "newest three not found" looks like allocation that partly succeeded and was then released: `allocate_pages_for_keys` is all-or-nothing per rank, so during a 5x flood some keys can fail to allocate (or their write can fail) and their pages return to the free list, leaving the newest prompts never complete - which a reader sees exactly as "not found". The alternative is that they completed and were then evicted; LRU makes that unlikely for the newest keys, but not impossible if allocation continued after them.

Two things from that window would separate the cases:
- any `Evicted key ...` lines between the flood and the check (eviction) versus none (never completed);
- whether the save-failure counter on the writing pod moved, and whether the miss was at the scheduler (`batch_key_exists` False: absent or partial) or in the worker (complete but pages gone).

If it is reproducible, I would rather add one debug-level log line, "eviction had no candidate" / "allocation failed after releasing pages", than grow the PR. Should I add that, or would you prefer the next run to start from c9b2b40 as is?

Thanks for the test and the docstring. On (2), our saved logs answer it: it was our test timing, not the PR.

- The writer's last 8 flood requests (they include the 3 newest prompts) were scheduled at 12:24:19-21 UTC. Their saves finished at 12:24:41-46 on all 4 ranks, 21-25 s later. During the flood the save queue fell behind the prefill.
- The reader checked the 3 newest prompts at 12:24:37-39 (15 s after the flood returned), while those saves were still queued. The reader's scheduler logged `0 matched (0 blocks)` for them, so the miss was at the scheduler (keys not complete yet), not in the worker.
- No save failed: `Num save task failed=0` in every writer metrics line of that window (12:24:15, :25, :35, :45), and no `Page allocation failed` or other error line on the writer.
- The metadata server logged `Evicted key` lines until 12:24:48, which matches the late saves.

So no debug line is needed for this, and c9b2b40 as is is fine for us. In a next run we will wait until the writer's save queue is empty before we check.

One side fact from the same window: the reader computed those 3 prompts and saved them itself at 12:24:38-40, while the writer's saves of the same prompts were still queued (they completed later). We saw no errors from this double write; we did not check which copy the metadata server kept.

Thanks - the log timeline closes it. "Scheduler logged 0 matched blocks while the saves were still queued, no save failures, and `Evicted key` kept appearing until 12:24:48" is exactly the case the design skips: a key that is not complete yet is never an eviction candidate, so the reader sees "not present" rather than "evicted". Nothing to add on our side, and c9b2b40 stays as is; no debug line.

On the side fact (reader computing and saving the same three prompts while the writer's saves were queued): the metadata server has no writer lease, so what happened is the documented cache-hit path, not a bug. `allocate_pages_for_keys` returns the existing page for a complete key (`cached_pages`), so the second writer gets the same page and writes into it instead of allocating a new one - which is why you saw no leaked page, no allocation failure and no error. `confirm_write_for_keys` is idempotent per (key, rank), so the second confirmation just re-records the same page.

What that does not give you is serialization: two writers can have those bytes in flight at the same time. For the same key the KV content should be identical (the key hashes model, tokens and block), so the outcome should be correct even if the writes interleave, but I cannot claim protection against a real content mismatch. If that ever shows up, the fix is a write lease like the read lease - deliberately out of scope here so the diff stays at one mechanism.

I updated the PR description-level notes in my own record; nothing in the code changed. Thanks again for spending two H100s on this - the leased-key and expired-lease rows are the ones I could not produce here.

@@ -177,6 +177,49 @@ def test_allocate_returns_minus_one_when_pool_exhausted(self):
         # allocate_pages uses all-or-nothing: 2 needed but only 1 available → []
         assert all(v == -1 for v in results.values()), f"Expected all -1, got {results}"
 
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("cached_first", [True, False])
+    def test_mixed_batch_uses_capacity_only_for_misses(self, cached_first):
+        """A cache hit must not prevent an otherwise fitting new allocation."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 2)
+        cached_page = state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("cached", "")])["cached"]
+        state.confirm_write_for_keys(0, [("cached", cached_page)])
+
+        keys = [("cached", ""), ("new", "")]
+        if not cached_first:
+            keys.reverse()
+        results = state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, keys)

+        assert results["cached"] == cached_page
+        assert results["new"] >= 0
+        assert results["new"] != cached_page
+        assert state.rank_metadata[0].get_free_page_count() == 0
+
+    def test_insufficient_misses_preserve_cached_page_and_free_capacity(self):
+        """An oversized miss batch must not consume pages or invalidate hits."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 2)
+        cached_page = state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("cached", "")])["cached"]
+        state.confirm_write_for_keys(0, [("cached", cached_page)])
+
+        results = state.allocate_pages_for_keys(
+            0, [("new_a", ""), ("cached", ""), ("new_b", "")]
+        )
+
+        assert results == {"new_a": -1, "cached": cached_page, "new_b": -1}
+        assert state.get_key_locations(0, ["cached"]) == [cached_page]
+        assert state.rank_metadata[0].get_free_page_count() == 1
+
+    def test_duplicate_new_key_consumes_one_page(self):
+        """The key-based allocation response must not orphan a duplicate's page."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 2)
+
+        results = state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("new", ""), ("new", "")])
+
+        assert results == {"new": 0}
+        assert state.rank_metadata[0].get_free_page_count() == 1

         free_after_release = state.rank_metadata[0].get_free_page_count()
 
         assert free_after_release == free_after_alloc + 1
+
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# TestGlobalMetadataStateEviction
+# ===========================================================================
+
+
+def _fill(state, keys, pages):
+    """Write `keys` into pre-selected pages so the free pool is empty."""
+    state.rank_metadata[0].free_pages = [
+        p for p in state.rank_metadata[0].free_pages if p not in pages
+    ]
+    for key, page in zip(keys, pages):
+        state.confirm_write_for_keys(0, [(key, page)])
+
+
+class TestGlobalMetadataStateEviction:
+    """Tests for LRU eviction, reader leases, and the unchanged all-or-nothing."""
+
+    def test_eviction_frees_page_for_new_key(self):
+        """A full pool with an unleased complete key makes room for a new key."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 2)
+        _fill(state, ["K1", "K2"], [0, 1])
+        assert state.rank_metadata[0].get_free_page_count() == 0
+
+        results = state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("K3", "")])
+
+        assert results["K3"] == 0, results  # oldest key's page was reclaimed
+        assert state.batch_key_exists(["K1"]) == [False]
+        assert state.get_key_locations(0, ["K1"]) == [None]
+        assert state.evicted_keys == 1
+
+    def test_leased_key_is_not_evicted(self):
+        """A key held by a reader survives eviction; allocation fails instead."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 1)
+        _fill(state, ["K1"], [0])
+
+        assert state.acquire_keys(0, ["K1"]) == {"K1": 0}
+        assert state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("K2", "")]) == {"K2": -1}
+        assert state.batch_key_exists(["K1"]) == [True]
+
+        state.release_keys(0, ["K1"])
+        assert state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("K2", "")]) == {"K2": 0}
+
+    def test_overlapping_leases_keep_the_key_pinned(self):
+        """One reader releasing must not unpin a key another reader still holds."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 1)
+        _fill(state, ["K1"], [0])
+
+        state.acquire_keys(0, ["K1"], ttl_s=10.0)
+        state.acquire_keys(0, ["K1"], ttl_s=1e6)  # a second, later reader
+        state.release_keys(0, ["K1"])  # only the first reader is done
+
+        assert state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("K2", "")]) == {"K2": -1}
+
+        state.release_keys(0, ["K1"])
+        assert state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("K2", "")]) == {"K2": 0}
+
+    def test_expired_lease_is_reclaimed(self):
+        """A lease from a crashed reader expires instead of pinning pages."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 1)
+        _fill(state, ["K1"], [0])
+
+        state.acquire_keys(0, ["K1"], ttl_s=-1.0)  # already expired
+        assert state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("K2", "")]) == {"K2": 0}
+        assert state.batch_key_exists(["K1"]) == [False]
+
+    def test_eviction_skips_partial_keys(self):
+        """A key without a confirmed write is never reclaimed by eviction."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 2)
+        partial_page = state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("partial", "")])["partial"]
+        _fill(state, ["done"], [1])
+
+        results = state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("new", "")])
+
+        assert results["new"] == 1
+        # The partial key still owns its page: only the complete key was evicted.
+        assert state.rank_metadata[0].get_free_page_count() == 0
+        assert state.batch_key_exists(["partial"]) == [False]
+        assert state.get_key_locations(0, ["partial"]) == [None]
+        assert partial_page == 0
+
+    def test_hits_of_the_allocating_request_are_not_evicted(self):
+        """Pages a request is about to read from cache must not be recycled."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 2)
+        _fill(state, ["K1", "K2"], [0, 1])
+
+        results = state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("K1", ""), ("K3", "")])
+
+        assert results["K1"] == 0
+        assert results["K3"] == 1
+        assert state.batch_key_exists(["K1"]) == [True]
+        assert state.batch_key_exists(["K2"]) == [False]
+
+    def test_eviction_prefers_least_recently_used(self):
+        """Acquiring a key refreshes its LRU position."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 2)
+        _fill(state, ["K1", "K2"], [0, 1])

+        state.acquire_keys(0, ["K1"])
+        state.release_keys(0, ["K1"])

+        assert state.batch_key_exists(["K1"]) == [True]
+        assert state.batch_key_exists(["K2"]) == [False]
+
+    def test_eviction_across_ranks_releases_every_page(self):
+        """Evicting a key returns one page per rank, keeping the pools disjoint."""
+        state = GlobalMetadataState()
+        state.initialize_rank(0, 1)
+        state.initialize_rank(1, 1)
+        state.confirm_write_for_keys(0, [("K", 0)])
+        state.confirm_write_for_keys(1, [("K", 0)])
+        assert state.batch_key_exists(["K"]) == [True]
+
+        assert state.allocate_pages_for_keys(0, [("K2", "")]) == {"K2": 0}
+
+        assert state.rank_metadata[0].get_free_page_count() == 0
+        assert state.rank_metadata[1].get_free_page_count() == 1
+        assert state.rank_metadata[1].free_pages == [0]

🚀

Test results on real 3FS, as offered in #62389.

**Setup:** vLLM v0.32.0 with the two changed files of this PR at `ed8a5db` (the PR base is identical to v0.32.0 for these files), plus the one-line metadata URL fix from #62465 (without it each instance talks to a localhost metadata server). Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, TP4, block size 64. Two instances on two H100 hosts (pod A writes, pod B reads), one shared metadata server (this PR's file, default lease TTL 120 s), 3FS over FUSE with USRBIO. Small pool on purpose: `hf3fs_file_size` 2 GiB per rank = 409 pages per rank. Needle prompts of about 1,850 tokens with one known answer each; flood prompts of 3,256 tokens (50 new keys each).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Before the pool is full | B loaded A's prompts from 3FS (1,792 of 1,850 tokens), answers correct |
| Sequential flood past the pool (12 prompts) | each prompt evicted exactly 50 keys; free pages stayed 0 on all 4 ranks; B loaded the 3 newest prompts from 3FS (3,200 tokens each) |
| Concurrent flood (12 prompts, 8 at a time) | B loaded the 3 newest prompts from 3FS (3,200 tokens each) |
| New prompts after the pool is full | 4 of 4 stored and loaded by B from 3FS (1,792-1,856 tokens), answers correct |
| Old prompts | stored before the flood: evicted (0 tokens from 3FS on B), answers correct (recomputed) |
| Lease protects keys | I held a lease with `POST /keys/acquire` on all 4 ranks for one prompt's 29 keys and never released it (a stalled reader), then flooded: an unleased control prompt had 0 of 29 keys left, the leased prompt 29 of 29; B loaded the leased prompt from 3FS (1,792 tokens), answer correct |
| Expired lease | 134 s after the acquire, the next flood evicted the leased prompt (0 of 29 keys), `leased` count 0 |
| Errors | 0 failed saves and 0 failed loads in the vLLM KV transfer metrics on both instances; 0 wrong answers in 28 needle checks |

Two observations:

1. The lease deadline is the latest deadline of all leases on a key. B read the leased prompt about 10 s after my acquire, so at 125 s 28 of the 29 keys still counted as leased, and they were evicted at 134 s. So a lease that is never released lasts until no reader has touched the key for one TTL. I think that is fine; it may be worth a line in the docs.
2. Seen once and not reproduced: 15 s after a larger concurrent flood (60 prompts, 8 at a time, about 5 x the pool), B found none of the 3 newest prompts, and free pages were 100 on rank 0 and 50 on ranks 1-3. The 12-prompt floods above did not show it. Saves may still have been in progress; I did not prove the cause.

Not covered: a real reader process killed in the middle of a read (I simulated the stalled reader with `/keys/acquire`), and throughput impact.

Thanks for running this on real 3FS with two hosts - that covers the two things I could not test here (two writers, one metadata server, and a pool that actually fills). The numbers answer what a single-host harness cannot: each flood prompt evicting exactly its 50 keys, 0/29 unleased vs 29/29 leased surviving, and the expired lease reclaimed on the next flood.

On (1): you are right, and it is now written down. Leases are counted per key, and a key stays pinned until the latest deadline among its live leases, so one reader releasing does not unpin it for another reader. Your 125 s observation is the same rule seen from the other side: pod B's read at ~10 s refreshed the deadline, so the pin lasted until last-touch + TTL, not acquire + TTL. I added that sentence to `acquire_keys` and a test (`test_overlapping_leases_keep_the_key_pinned`: acquire with 10 s, then 1e6 s, release the first, require that allocation still fails; release the second, require that it succeeds). Pushed as c9b2b40 - docstring and test only, no behaviour change, so the sha moves from ed8a5db to c9b2b40. Local isolated harness: 26 passed, ruff clean. Any test you re-run on c9b2b40 is testing the same code paths.

On (2) I do not have a proven explanation either. The 100/50 free-page split plus "newest three not found" looks like allocation that partly succeeded and was then released: `allocate_pages_for_keys` is all-or-nothing per rank, so during a 5x flood some keys can fail to allocate (or their write can fail) and their pages return to the free list, leaving the newest prompts never complete - which a reader sees exactly as "not found". The alternative is that they completed and were then evicted; LRU makes that unlikely for the newest keys, but not impossible if allocation continued after them.

Two things from that window would separate the cases:
- any `Evicted key ...` lines between the flood and the check (eviction) versus none (never completed);
- whether the save-failure counter on the writing pod moved, and whether the miss was at the scheduler (`batch_key_exists` False: absent or partial) or in the worker (complete but pages gone).

If it is reproducible, I would rather add one debug-level log line, "eviction had no candidate" / "allocation failed after releasing pages", than grow the PR. Should I add that, or would you prefer the next run to start from c9b2b40 as is?

Thanks for the test and the docstring. On (2), our saved logs answer it: it was our test timing, not the PR.

- The writer's last 8 flood requests (they include the 3 newest prompts) were scheduled at 12:24:19-21 UTC. Their saves finished at 12:24:41-46 on all 4 ranks, 21-25 s later. During the flood the save queue fell behind the prefill.
- The reader checked the 3 newest prompts at 12:24:37-39 (15 s after the flood returned), while those saves were still queued. The reader's scheduler logged `0 matched (0 blocks)` for them, so the miss was at the scheduler (keys not complete yet), not in the worker.
- No save failed: `Num save task failed=0` in every writer metrics line of that window (12:24:15, :25, :35, :45), and no `Page allocation failed` or other error line on the writer.
- The metadata server logged `Evicted key` lines until 12:24:48, which matches the late saves.

So no debug line is needed for this, and c9b2b40 as is is fine for us. In a next run we will wait until the writer's save queue is empty before we check.

One side fact from the same window: the reader computed those 3 prompts and saved them itself at 12:24:38-40, while the writer's saves of the same prompts were still queued (they completed later). We saw no errors from this double write; we did not check which copy the metadata server kept.

Thanks - the log timeline closes it. "Scheduler logged 0 matched blocks while the saves were still queued, no save failures, and `Evicted key` kept appearing until 12:24:48" is exactly the case the design skips: a key that is not complete yet is never an eviction candidate, so the reader sees "not present" rather than "evicted". Nothing to add on our side, and c9b2b40 stays as is; no debug line.

On the side fact (reader computing and saving the same three prompts while the writer's saves were queued): the metadata server has no writer lease, so what happened is the documented cache-hit path, not a bug. `allocate_pages_for_keys` returns the existing page for a complete key (`cached_pages`), so the second writer gets the same page and writes into it instead of allocating a new one - which is why you saw no leaked page, no allocation failure and no error. `confirm_write_for_keys` is idempotent per (key, rank), so the second confirmation just re-records the same page.

What that does not give you is serialization: two writers can have those bytes in flight at the same time. For the same key the KV content should be identical (the key hashes model, tokens and block), so the outcome should be correct even if the writes interleave, but I cannot claim protection against a real content mismatch. If that ever shows up, the fix is a write lease like the read lease - deliberately out of scope here so the diff stays at one mechanism.

I updated the PR description-level notes in my own record; nothing in the code changed. Thanks again for spending two H100s on this - the leased-key and expired-lease rows are the ones I could not produce here.
